messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: GPU pool 'eu-west-1-pool-B' saturated, queue growth > 1200 reqs/min, throttling observed. Severity: P1. Links: https://alerts.redwood.example/1915001234

Elaine: saw this spike, I'm paged. customer-facing latency > 10s for some requests, errors are 429/504. tagging @SRE-Oncall

SRE-Oncall: I'm on it. grabbing recent autoscale events and pool status. If autoscaler didn't act we may have a config regression.

Priya: current autoscale policy shows max_replicas=64, last scale event 1915000820 backoff: 5m. But GPU scheduler indicates OOMs on new instances, pods stuck in "Pending" due to quota.

Omar: confirming: quota errors in cluster events: 
```
Warning  FailedCreate  2m kubelet  failed to create pod: Insufficient accelerators (nvidia.com/gpu)
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

Kevin: hmm autoscaler kept requesting nodes but cloud quota for GPUs in eu-west-1 is at limit (customer-wide commit + on-demand). I just checked billing/limits console.

Nathan: aside from quota, we're also seeing a large increase in prefix cache misses on the model hot-path. TTL for prefix cache recently changed in the canary to 60s -> 0 (disable) at 1914998000. Could be causing more work per request and increasing token compute.

Elaine: @Nathan that's our suspicion too — more cold KV lookups means longer runtimes, keeping GPUs busy -> slower throughput -> queue pile-up. Any way to revert that TTL quickly?

SRE-Oncall: Immediate mitigations: 1) Re-enable prefix cache on serving tier (rollback canary). 2) If quota prevents autoscale, temporarily shift traffic to a compatible variant with lower GPU memory (quantized model). 3) Manually increase queue throttle to shed non-critical workloads. Who can run the rollback?

Priya: I can rollback the canary through infra console. Doing it now: `infra rollback service/redwood-prefix-cache-canary --to=1914996000`

Priya: rollback initiated, pods recycling. ETA ~60s for new caches to populate.

Omar: I'll validate pool capacity and attempt a manual scale up with a different instance type (if cloud permits): `cloudcli compute quota-request --region=eu-west-1 --accelerator=nvidia-a100 --count=8`

Kevin: I've opened a ticket with cloud support to increase GPU quota, but that's slow. For now I can route 30% of incoming traffic to deduped quantized variant (model-small-q8) from the router to reduce pressure. Patching route now.

SRE-Oncall: Patch to router accepted, shifting 30% to model-small-q8. Watch for any QA/customer regressions. Also raising throttle config: `max_inflight_per_key=4` to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Nathan: prefix cache rollback finished on canary and start propagating. Early metrics: prefix cache hit rate climbing from 12% -> 78% in 90s, p99 latency on GPU requests falling from 6.8s -> 2.1s.

CS-Bot: Notifying impacted customers with templated message: "We experienced elevated latency for inference in eu-west-1. We've applied mitigations; we will follow up with root cause and timeline." (sent to customers with >5% error rate)

Elaine: queue length trending down from 4k -> 600 in past 4m. Autoscaler still blocked by quota but pressure relieved by cache rollback + traffic shift.

SRE-Oncall: Good. Next steps: 1) follow-up on why prefix-cache TTL change rolled to canary without perf guardrail in rollout. 2) investigate release pipeline approval that allowed TTL=0. 3) add an autoscale fallback to allow routing to other regions when local quota is exhausted. Assigning: Nathan -> cache rollout RCA, Kevin -> cloud quota escalation / routing fallback design, Priya -> rollout pipeline guardrails.

Nathan: noted, will pull logs and create an eval dashboard comparing canary vs baseline for prefix-cache.

Kevin: I'll keep the temporary 30% route in place and monitor error budgets. If quota increase comes in we can revert.

SRE-Oncall: Incident status -> mitigated at 1915001500. Monitoring until 1915001578 then handoff to postmortem. Paging SRE rotation ~ next 2 hours for post-incident. Nice work everyone. :tada:
